messages:
Erin (AE): Heads up — Ardent wants to run a 6-week POC next month. main asks: onboard a custom 30B variant, KV cache behavior, and pricing guidance for a reserved bucket. Can we check gaps?
Sam (Eng-ML): Quick Q — is this their fork of LlamaX or something custom from their team?
Erin (AE): It's their in-house tuned fork, calls it 'ardent-30b-tuned-v2'. They provided a model tar and weights.
Mike (Solutions): We should run a compatibility scan: tokenizer, attention layout, state_dict keys. If it's a standard HF checkpoint probably fine, but tuned checkpoints sometimes rename modules.
Sam (Eng-ML): Agree. I can do an initial model loader pass. Need the tar and a sample config. Also: sequence length distribution and typical prompt shapes.
Erin (AE): I already asked them for a 500-sample prompt set and the tar link. Expecting it tomorrow.
Hana (Security): Heads-up: Ardent is HIPAA-scoped. They'll require KMS integration, SOC2 attestation in our contract, and an option for private deployment (VPC). We need to surface any data egress risks for the POC.
Rebecca (Sales Ops): Pricing flag: they asked about reserved capacity for the POC: estimate 20M tokens/month steady with spikes. They want a price for dedicated pool + engineering onboarding support.
Oliver (Infra): For dedicated pool we need to know GPU profile: fp16 or int8 quant? If they need int8 we'll need to validate quantization artifacts. Dedicated nodes + burst capacity is doable but lead time is ~2 weeks to reserve infra.
Julia (Product): Add-on: can we offer a canary fallback to an open 30B variant if the tuned one fails? That eases SLA risk.
Mike (Solutions): Canary sounds good. We should also plan for automatic fallback to lower-memory variant to avoid OOM on long prefixes.
Sam (Eng-ML): Technical plan I propose: 1) ingest tar into a sandbox, run model loader. 2) run unit generation tests with their 500 prompts. 3) run perf sweep (latency/cost) across sequence lengths. 4) KV cache sanity + prefix reuse test.
Erin (AE): Can someone own the scan? I can coordinate with Ardent for credentials.
Sam (Eng-ML): I'll own the scan. tag: Sam. Need tar URL, example prompts, and a short eval harness (python script) or I'll stub one.
Hana (Security): I'll start the security checklist. Preliminary blockers: 1) they want BYOK with customer-managed keys — we support KMS but need to confirm HSM/BYOK specifics. 2) SSO/SCIM for access provision during POC. 3) Data retention export rules for HIPAA.
Rebecca (Sales Ops): For pricing: I'll draft two options — (A) Dedicated small pool + premium onboarding: fixed monthly + token overage; (B) Hosted with dedicated SLA + higher per-token. Which do we prefer for RFP?
Erin (AE): They asked for committed pricing (month-to-month for POC) but are open to an annual if POC successful. Let's prepare both.
Oliver (Infra): Note: if we enable KV cache across requests for efficiency, we must confirm whether their prompts include PII — cache retention and encryption at rest need to be explicit in MSA.
Hana (Security): Exactly. Also need clarity on where the cache persists (ephemeral RAM vs disk). We should document our default: in-memory KV with optional persisted prefix cache on disk only for Dedicated/Private and encrypted with KMS.
Mike (Solutions): Small snippet we might run for the model loader:
```
# quick sanity load
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer
model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained('path/to/ardent-30b-tuned-v2')
tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('path/to/ardent-30b-tuned-v2')
print(tokenizer.decode(tokenizer('hello world')['input_ids']))
```
Sam (Eng-ML): Nice. Also will test kv-cache hit-rate by sending repeated prefixes and measuring token generation time delta.
Erin (AE): Action items so far: Sam = compatibility + perf scan; Hana = security checklist + KMS/BYOK ask; Rebecca = draft pricing options; Oliver = infra lead for dedicated provisioning; Mike = fallback plan doc; Erin = coordinate with customer and procure sample data.
Julia (Product): For the catalog side: if scan passes, we'll create an 'ardent-30b-tuned-v2' variant entry with metadata: quant levels tested, recommended batch sizes, recommended kv-cache settings, and a fallbacks list. Product will own the metadata entry.
Hana (Security): Also add a note: any PHI that flows to log/observability must be redacted; we can enable minimal telemetry in the POC.
Rebecca (Sales Ops): Estimated term & pricing draft due by EOD Friday. Sam, can you give an ETA on the scan?
Sam (Eng-ML): If I get the tar + sample prompts by tomorrow noon I can run the loader + basic perf by Thurs EOD. Full sweep Friday.
Erin (AE): I'll ask Ardent to provide artifacts this afternoon.
sec-bot: Security checklist created: https://internal/redwood/sec-checks/ardent-poc (private link) :lock:
Mike (Solutions): One more blocker to flag: procurement asked about export controls for the model weights. If their model includes third-party licensed layers we need a compliance review.
Erin (AE): Good catch. I'll add that to the docs request list.
Oliver (Infra): If we need private deployment for HIPAA, lead time + contract change — call it ~4 weeks. POC timeline might need adjustment.
Erin (AE): Noted. I'll surface that to the customer.
Rebecca (Sales Ops): I'll assemble the commercial options and SLA deltas. Putting draft in GDrive and sharing in this thread when ready.
Sam (Eng-ML): I'll post results as a short summary: compatibility (ok/fail), perf numbers (p95 latency, tokens/sec), kv-cache hit rate, memory footprint.
Erin (AE): Thanks team. Quick follow-up: if anyone needs additional resources or test accounts let me know here. I'll ping Ardent for the artifacts now.
Julia (Product): If scan is green, product will fast-track catalog onboarding to staging so Solutions can test routing policies for canary/fallback.
Rebecca (Sales Ops): FYI I added a procurement checkbox for export license review.
Hana (Security): I'll need the sample prompts before I sign off on telemetry settings.
Erin (AE): Got it. I'll push for same-day upload.
Sam (Eng-ML): Cool — will standby.
Erin (AE): Closing note — tagging for awareness: @everyone in #sales-ops for timelines.
